pageTitle: Amparo — Know your rights at every traffic stop.
doc_link: Why can't practice make a stop 100% safe? →
doc_title: The truth we can't practice away
doc_h: Some people did everything right and were still killed.
doc_body: We don't ask you to take our word for it — here are documented cases, with sources you can read yourself:
doc_case1_body: During a 2016 traffic stop in Minnesota he calmly told the officer he had a licensed firearm, exactly as advised, and was shot and killed. The officer was acquitted in 2017.
doc_case2_body: A 2021 traffic stop in Brooklyn Center, Minnesota ended when an officer shot and killed him. She was later convicted of manslaughter.
doc_blame: This is a failure of the system and the officer — never of the person who was killed.
doc_why: We show you this not to scare you, but because a tool that promised words could keep you safe would be lying to you — and because you deserve to see where the facts come from.
doc_clarity: Practicing calm, minimal responses measurably lowers how threatening you appear to an officer — that much is documented. It cannot make you safe, because the risk was never fully in your hands. Knowing that isn't despair — it's clarity: do your part, and put the blame where it belongs.
doc_resource: If this brings up grief or fear, you're not alone. Call or text 988 (free, 24/7, confidential). For your rights, contact your local ACLU affiliate: aclu.org/affiliates.

ab_mission: Too many drivers have to plan for a traffic stop going wrong. Amparo — Spanish for shelter — turns your rights into something you can hold in your hand, so your hands stay on the wheel and the card does the talking.
ab_who_pending: Amparo is an independent project. Founder and team details are shown here before public launch.
ab_founder_note:
I built Amparo for anyone, of any minority, anywhere, who has ever feared that a routine stop could cost them their life. You deserve at least this: the knowledge, rehearsed and ready, so you have a fighting chance to make it home.

Do your part — stay calm, keep your hands visible, record what happens. If you do everything right and it still goes wrong, that record is yours: proof of how you carried yourself, so the truth can protect you and hold others accountable.

Whoever you are, reading this: I thought of you when I made this. I pray this never happens to you. But if it does, I hope you're armed with the right knowledge to move forward with your life.
ab_review_pending: Every rule in Amparo is cited to the exact state statute or code section — check the number yourself, anytime. We're also having each state's content formally reviewed and signed off by a licensed attorney in that state before public launch. Until a state shows a green “Attorney-reviewed” badge, treat it as well-sourced general information, not legal advice.
ab_state_pending: attorney sign-off in progress — rules already cited to statute
ab_privacy: Amparo works with no account at all, and that is the default. If you choose to create one to save your pack across devices, it stores only your pack's text — state, names, phone numbers, ZIP — on our server, and that record could be handed over if we were legally compelled. You can delete it at any time from the same screen. Your document photos and your practice history are never uploaded, with or without an account: there is nowhere on the server to put them. We count anonymous events (like how many packs get printed, and in which state) to prove the tool is used — never who you are, never what you typed, never your photos. If you send us feedback, what you write reaches us, plus your name and email only if you fill them in. We never sell or share anything with any agency, including immigration authorities.

prep_title: BEFORE YOU DRIVE — SET THESE IN PLACE

prep.en: Keep this card in your driver's door pocket or clipped to your visor — within one slow reach.
prep.es: Guarde esta tarjeta en el bolsillo de la puerta o en el visor — a un alcance lento.

prep.en: Tuck your real license, insurance & registration where the card shows them.
prep.es: Coloque su licencia, seguro y registro reales donde la tarjeta los muestra.

prep.en: Wallet card in your wallet. Emergency contact knows they're your call.
prep.es: Tarjeta de cartera en su cartera. Su contacto de emergencia lo sabe.

prep.en: Practice the 7 steps once with someone you trust.
prep.es: Practique los 7 pasos una vez con alguien de confianza.

prep.en: Print with “background graphics” ON, then keep this pack in a plastic sheet protector — a 10-cent raincoat.
prep.es: Imprima con “gráficos de fondo” activados y guarde el paquete en un protector de hojas — un impermeable de 10 centavos.

prep.en: Best upgrade: a $40 always-on dashcam — it records every stop with zero movement from you.
prep.es: La mejor mejora: una dashcam siempre encendida (~$40) — graba cada parada sin que usted se mueva.

steps.en: Signal, pull to the right, stop safely. Engine off, hazards on, music off, interior light at night.
steps.es: Señalice, hágase a la derecha y deténgase con seguridad. Motor apagado, intermitentes, música apagada, luz interior de noche.

steps.en: While pulling over: tap record, lay the phone on the dash or seat — never in your hand.
steps.es: Mientras se detiene: active la grabación y deje el teléfono en el tablero o el asiento — nunca en la mano.

steps.en: Before the officer arrives: card against the glass, window down 2–3 inches, then stop moving.
steps.es: Antes de que llegue el oficial: tarjeta contra el vidrio, ventana abajo 5–7 cm, y quieto.

steps.en: Both hands high on the wheel, in plain view. They stay there the whole stop.
steps.es: Ambas manos en alto sobre el volante, a la vista. Ahí se quedan toda la parada.

steps.en: Questioned? Say it out loud, once: “I’m not answering questions, officer.” Then silence — polite silence. Arrested? Add: “I want a lawyer.”
steps.es: ¿Le preguntan? Dígalo en voz alta, una vez: “No voy a responder preguntas, oficial.” Luego silencio — con cortesía. ¿Arrestado? Agregue: “Quiero un abogado.”

steps.en: Documents? Say “I’m reaching now,” move slowly, hand over, hands back. Ordered out or told to sign? Comply.
steps.es: ¿Documentos? Diga “voy a alcanzarlos,” muévase despacio, entréguelos, manos al volante. ¿Le ordenan salir o firmar? Cumpla.

steps.en: Get their info — on the recording. At a pause (documents back, or release) ask once: “Officer, your name and badge, please?” Refused? “No problem” — then read the nameplate and car number quietly into your camera. Every pushback reply: page 4.
steps.es: Sus datos — en la grabación. En una pausa (documentos devueltos, o al final) pregunte una vez: “Oficial, ¿su nombre y placa, por favor?” ¿Se negó? “No hay problema” — y lea la placa del uniforme y el número de patrulla en voz baja hacia su cámara. Cada respuesta: página 4.

pr_practice: Practice this once with someone you trust — before you drive.

rights.en: My documents are displayed here. I will hand them over on request — my hands are staying visible until then.
rights.es: Mis documentos están aquí. Los entregaré si me los pide — mis manos permanecen visibles.

rights.en: I do not consent to any search.
rights.es: No doy consentimiento para ningún registro.

rights.en: If I am being detained, please tell me why.
rights.es: Si estoy detenido/a, por favor dígame por qué.

rights.en: If I am not being detained, am I free to go?
